audit.whatIsWrong: Rated 5.5/10 even, but the win rate is 41.67% and the content layer's own late-game text says Neeko reclaims the matchup.
audit.why: Neeko has two hard-CC entries (Tangle-Barbs at 1000 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, and Pop Blossom's knockup-into-stun on 120/105/90s) plus Inherent Glamour disguises and Shapesplitter clones for ambush; Lillia has no dash or defensive button. The lane is even at best, and tilts once Neeko has items.
audit.corrected: Difficulty nudged to 6/10, carry threat 6.5/10; the chart now names Levels 3-5 as Lillia's real window and 2+ items as Neeko's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows were flat 'Skill' or misassigned: Levels 3 and 4-5 were marked Skill despite both layers describing them as Lillia's best window; Level 6 was marked Neeko despite the text saying the two ultimates cancel; 2+ items was Skill despite the text saying Neeko out-scales.
audit.why: Lillia's spike is Blooming Blows move-speed stacking plus the Dream Dust DoT at levels 3-5, when Neeko has neither clone nor Pop Blossom. Neeko's spike is her first AP item, which turns E-root into a burst combo.
audit.corrected: Rows set to Lillia (Lvl 3), Lillia (Lvls 4-5), Skill (Lvl 6), Neeko (2+ items) as matched full+content pairs, with ratings 6, 6, 5, 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 why claimed 'ganks are now guaranteed' and said nothing about the actual R-versus-R interaction, which is the decisive one at that level.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust from Lillia's passive, and Pop Blossom has a visible preparation before the leap — hidden only while Neeko is disguised. So the sleep answers her ult only if the DoT is already on her, which is exactly the sequencing a player needs told.
audit.corrected: Level 6 why rewritten to state the cancel and its Dream Dust precondition.
